comment: Rust-only commands appended to the 2.x catalog by update-catalog.sh: batch:* (cli#60), the task queue activity dispatch pause (task-queue:activity-dispatch, task-queue:pause-activities, task-queue:resume-activities; Server #577) and workflow:update-outcome (Server #1131, durable-workflow/.github#212). 2.x has no equivalent, so parity skips their help and strips them from listings.

commands.name: batch:cancel
commands.description: Cancel the workflows a visibility query selects, with a resumable manifest
commands.synopsis: batch:cancel [-s|--server [SERVER]] [--namespace [NAMESPACE]] [--token [TOKEN]] [--tls-verify TLS-VERIFY] [--env ENV] [--output OUTPUT] [--query QUERY] [-t|--type [TYPE]] [--status [STATUS]] [-l|--limit [LIMIT]] [--reason [REASON]] [--manifest MANIFEST] [--rate [RATE]] [--deadline DEADLINE] [-y|--yes] [--json]
commands.help:
Select up to <comment>--limit</comment> workflows with a visibility query, pin each to the run
the listing reported, and record the selection in a new private manifest
before cancelling anything. Each run is cancelled with exactly one request
and its outcome is recorded as it arrives. If the batch stops, resume it
with <comment>dw batch:resume</comment>: targets already done are never sent again, and a
target whose outcome is unknown is reported for inspection, never resent.
See docs/batch-operations.md for the manifest format and recovery steps.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw batch:cancel --query='customer-42' --manifest=cancel-42.jsonl</info>
  <info>dw batch:cancel --query='customer-42' --reason=offboarded --manifest=c.jsonl --yes --json</info>

commands.name: batch:signal
commands.description: Signal the workflows a visibility query selects, with a resumable manifest
commands.synopsis: batch:signal [-s|--server [SERVER]] [--namespace [NAMESPACE]] [--token [TOKEN]] [--tls-verify TLS-VERIFY] [--env ENV] [--output OUTPUT] [--query QUERY] [-t|--type [TYPE]] [--status [STATUS]] [-l|--limit [LIMIT]] [--manifest MANIFEST] [--rate [RATE]] [--deadline DEADLINE] [-y|--yes] [--json] [-i|--input [INPUT]] [--input-file [INPUT-FILE]] [--input-encoding [INPUT-ENCODING]] [--] <signal-name>
commands.help:
Select up to <comment>--limit</comment> workflows with a visibility query, pin each to the run
the listing reported, and record the selection, the signal and its input in
a new private manifest before sending anything. Each target gets its own
command key (<comment>request_id</comment>), reused unchanged on resume. A target whose
outcome is unknown is reported for inspection and never resent: a request ID
alone does not prove a repeated signal is safe.
See docs/batch-operations.md for the manifest format and recovery steps.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw batch:signal approve --query='queue-7' --manifest=approve.jsonl</info>
  <info>dw batch:signal payment_received --query='batch-9' -i '{"amount":10}' --manifest=pay.jsonl --yes</info>

commands.name: batch:update
commands.description: Send an update to the workflows a visibility query selects, with a resumable manifest
commands.synopsis: batch:update [-s|--server [SERVER]] [--namespace [NAMESPACE]] [--token [TOKEN]] [--tls-verify TLS-VERIFY] [--env ENV] [--output OUTPUT] [--query QUERY] [-t|--type [TYPE]] [--status [STATUS]] [-l|--limit [LIMIT]] [--wait [WAIT]] [--manifest MANIFEST] [--rate [RATE]] [--deadline DEADLINE] [-y|--yes] [--json] [-i|--input [INPUT]] [--input-file [INPUT-FILE]] [--input-encoding [INPUT-ENCODING]] [--] <update-name>
commands.help:
Select up to <comment>--limit</comment> workflows with a visibility query, pin each to the run
the listing reported, and record the selection, the update, its wait policy
and its input in a new private manifest before sending anything. Each target
gets its own command key (<comment>request_id</comment>), reused unchanged on resume. An
accepted or completed update is acknowledged; a rejected or failed one is
refused and never resent. A target whose outcome is unknown is reported for
inspection and never resent.
See docs/batch-operations.md for the manifest format and recovery steps.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw batch:update approve --query='queue-7' --manifest=approve.jsonl</info>
  <info>dw batch:update set-limit --query='tier-2' -i '{"limit":5}' --wait=completed --manifest=limits.jsonl --yes</info>

commands.name: batch:resume
commands.description: Continue a batch from its manifest without relisting or resending
commands.help:
Continue the targets of a recorded batch that have no definite outcome:
never dispatched, refused for authentication, or still under Server pressure.
Resume never relists, so it never retargets a successor run, and it reuses
each target's command key. It never resends acknowledged, refused, skipped
or unknown targets. The connection must name the same Server and namespace
the batch recorded.
See docs/batch-operations.md for the manifest format and recovery steps.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw batch:resume cancel-42.jsonl</info>
  <info>dw batch:resume approve.jsonl --yes --json</info>

commands.name: task-queue:activity-dispatch
commands.description: Show whether activity dispatch on a task queue is paused
commands.help:
Show whether activity dispatch on one task queue of the selected namespace
is paused, with the last pause (reason, when and by whom) and, once it
ended, its resume. <info>dw task-queue:describe</info> and <info>dw task-queue:list</info> also
show the state when the Server reports it.

Needs a Server that advertises the task_queue_activity_dispatch_pause
capability (native Server 3.8.0 or later). dw reads cluster info first
and refuses with exit 8, without sending the request, when it is
missing; published PHP Server 2.x has no activity dispatch pause.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw task-queue:activity-dispatch orders</info>
  <info>dw task-queue:activity-dispatch orders --json | jq '.activity_dispatch.state'</info>

commands.name: task-queue:pause-activities
commands.description: Pause activity dispatch on a task queue
commands.help:
Hold every new activity lease on one task queue of the selected namespace
until <info>dw task-queue:resume-activities</info> lifts the pause. The queue name
is compared byte for byte, and a queue need not exist yet.

While the queue is paused:

  - no activity task on it is leased; ready tasks stay ready and keep
    their attempt count, and activity polls come back empty;
  - activities already running keep running, and their heartbeats,
    completions and failures are accepted;
  - activity deadlines keep running: a schedule-to-start or
    schedule-to-close deadline that passes times the activity out;
  - workflow tasks, signals, queries and updates are delivered as before.

Pausing is idempotent: pausing a paused queue changes nothing and reports
the original pause. It is not a build-id drain (use
<info>dw task-queue:drain</info> to stop one build's workers) and not a concurrency
cap.

Needs a Server that advertises the task_queue_activity_dispatch_pause
capability (native Server 3.8.0 or later). dw reads cluster info first
and refuses with exit 8, without sending the request, when it is
missing; published PHP Server 2.x has no activity dispatch pause.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw task-queue:pause-activities orders --reason="payments vendor outage"</info>
  <info>dw task-queue:pause-activities orders --json</info>

commands.name: task-queue:resume-activities
commands.description: Resume activity dispatch on a paused task queue
commands.help:
Lift the activity dispatch pause on one task queue of the selected
namespace. Held activity polls on the node that serves the resume wake at
once; polls held on other nodes see it at their next readiness read.
Ready tasks are then leased as the attempt they would have been. An
activity that timed out during the pause stays timed out.

Resuming is idempotent: resuming a queue that is not paused changes
nothing. This does not touch build-id drains; use
<info>dw task-queue:resume</info> for those.

Needs a Server that advertises the task_queue_activity_dispatch_pause
capability (native Server 3.8.0 or later). dw reads cluster info first
and refuses with exit 8, without sending the request, when it is
missing; published PHP Server 2.x has no activity dispatch pause.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw task-queue:resume-activities orders</info>
  <info>dw task-queue:resume-activities orders --json</info>

commands.name: workflow:update-outcome
commands.description: Read an update's outcome later by its update ID
commands.help:
Read the outcome of an update sent earlier, by its update ID, without sending
the update again. The answer is the update's receipt:

  - accepted: admitted and not finished yet. This is a pending update, never
    a null result; run the command again with <comment>--wait=completed</comment> to wait.
  - completed: the handler returned. Its result envelope may encode null.
  - failed: the handler failed. dw prints the failure message and exits 2.
  - rejected: the Server's original rejection, with its exit code.

<comment>--wait=accepted</comment> (the default) answers at once. <comment>--wait=completed</comment> waits
for the outcome, up to <comment>--wait-timeout</comment> seconds or the Server's update wait
default, and still answers accepted if the update has not finished by then.

An update ID the Server does not retain for the workflow exits 5
(update_not_found). That does not prove the update was never admitted: a
retained update is pruned with its run. The update follows its workflow
across continue-as-new, so the Run ID shown is the run that owns it now.

Needs a Server that advertises the update_outcome_reads capability (native
Server 3.6.0 or later). dw reads cluster info first and refuses with exit 8,
without sending any request, when it is missing. dw never sends the update
again in place of a read.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw workflow:update-outcome chk-42 01JUPDATE00000000000000000</info>
  <info>dw workflow:update-outcome chk-42 01JUPDATE00000000000000000 --wait=completed --wait-timeout=30</info>
  <info>dw workflow:update-outcome chk-42 01JUPDATE00000000000000000 --json | jq '.update_status'</info>
